content_voiceover: Let's cover cold agglutinin disease lab findings and transfusion strategy, a classic board topic. Two values matter most. Antibody titer correlates with clinical severity: the diagnostic threshold is 64, but titers above 512 are considered clinically significant. Thermal amplitude is actually the better predictor of hemolysis, it's the highest temperature at which the antibody still binds red cell antigen. Clinically significant cold agglutinins typically exceed a thermal amplitude of 28 to 30 degrees Celsius, which is why labs test at 4, 22, and 37 degrees. For transfusion, remember, never withhold transfusion when it's indicated. Three practical fixes solve most interference. Prewarming technique resolves the majority of cases, with DTT reserved for difficult ones. Use a standard blood warmer set to 37 degrees during transfusion. And keep the patient warm, especially in cold weather, to reduce further agglutination.
keypoints: Diagnostic titer threshold is 64; titers above 512 are clinically significant
Thermal amplitude above 28 to 30 degrees C predicts hemolysis better than titer
Never withhold transfusion when clinically indicated
Prewarming resolves most interference; DTT for refractory cases
Use a 37 degree blood warmer and keep the patient warm
